source.title: Eigenvalue Distribution of Large Random Matrices Arising in Deep Neural Networks: Orthogonal Case

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; minor extraction/OCR notation glitches do not prevent reading the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves a large-width spectral-distribution result for Jacobians of untrained networks with orthogonal weights and Gaussian biases. This bears on the dynamical-isometry motivation in V4, but it does not test gradient training speed or trainable depth directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports mathematical results about Jacobian singular-value distributions for untrained networks. It does not report classification training-error outcomes on benchmarks. Statements about training efficiency and initialization in the introduction cite prior work and are not this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The paper proves a spectral-distribution theorem for untrained networks, rather than testing any version's training outcomes. Its statements connecting dynamical isometry to faster training are attributed to prior work. Jacobian conditioning alone does not establish learning speed or trainable depth in V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. More precisely, the theorem concerns eigenvalues of JJᵀ, equivalently squared singular values of the Jacobian. It rigorously justifies prior limiting spectral formulas for Haar orthogonal weights and Gaussian biases, including almost-sure convergence, without establishing training-speed or training-error results.
record.recipe_differences: Analytical random-matrix proof for untrained networks with orthogonal weights and Gaussian biases; no gradient-training experiment or benchmark recipe.
record.method_sensitivity: The limiting Jacobian distribution depends on network depth, activation derivative distribution, and the layerwise variance recurrence; no comparative training outcome is measured.

fits_no_version.finding: Theorem 2.1 establishes almost-sure convergence of the empirical eigenvalue distribution of JJᵀ to a deterministic free multiplicative convolution at infinite width and fixed depth, under Haar orthogonal weights, Gaussian biases and the stated activation and input assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For these untrained networks, the limiting Jacobian spectrum agrees with the formula obtained by replacing weight-dependent derivative matrices with suitable weight-independent counterparts.

record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Mathematics and Physics (as supplied in the study metadata)
record.problems: No empirical training outcomes or benchmark training-error measurements. The result is asymptotic in width and assumes bounded activation and derivative, Haar orthogonal weights, Gaussian biases, and a stated input-norm limit.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying rows: the paper's own results concern asymptotic spectral measures, which do not measure training error, initialization-driven learning speed, or trainable depth named in the versions. Training-efficiency statements in the introduction refer to cited work.

untested.parts: Training classification error, including corrupted or random labels, and dependence on size, stopping or regularization.
Teacher-student optimization, spurious local minima and the effect of extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training error and comparisons involving identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Initialization effects on learning speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian training comparisons and very deep convolutional training.
Learning-rate stability thresholds, loss recovery, curvature dynamics and divergence during training.
Batch normalization effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparisons with Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: Change the record's V4 status from tested_not_extracted to not_tested. The spectral results are already declared in rows_left_out, so no missing qualifying result rows are required.

versions.untested_parts: Training error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, model size, stopping, and regularization are not tested.
No teacher-student optimization or spurious-minimum outcomes are tested.
No plain versus residual network training-error comparison is tested.
The paper examines orthogonal weights and Jacobian singular-value distributions in untrained networks, but does not compare initialization methods for learning speed or trainable depth.
No learning-rate stability or loss-curvature training dynamics are tested.
Batch normalization and training speed or learning-rate tolerance are not tested.
